metadata.title: On Serre's reciprocity conjecture for 2-dimensional mod $p$ representations of $\mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$

nodes.name: Serre type representation
nodes.statement: An irreducible 2-dimensional odd mod $p$ representation $\bar{\rho}: \mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q}) \to GL_2(\mathbb{F})$ with $\mathbb{F}$ a finite field of characteristic $p$.
nodes.statement_clean: An odd irreducible 2-dim mod p Galois representation; called level 1 if unramified outside p.

nodes.name: Lift of $\bar{\rho}$
nodes.statement: A continuous representation $\rho: G_{\mathbb{Q}} \to \mathrm{GL}_2(\mathcal{O})$, with $\mathcal{O}$ the ring of integers of a finite extension of $\mathrm{Frac}(W(\mathbb{F}))$, whose reduction mod the maximal ideal of $\mathcal{O}$ is isomorphic to $\bar{\rho}$.

nodes.name: Minimally ramified lift at $\ell$
nodes.statement: For $\ell \neq p$: minimal in the sense of [DDT, D97]; if $\bar{\rho}$ unramified at $\ell$, so is $\rho$. For $\ell = p$: if $k(\bar{\rho}) \neq p+1$, $\rho$ is crystalline of weights $(0, k(\bar{\rho})-1)$; if $k(\bar{\rho}) = p+1$, semistable type means semistable non-crystalline of Hodge-Tate weights $(0,1)$, crystalline type means crystalline of weights $(0,p)$.

nodes.name: Minimally ramified deformation
nodes.statement: A deformation $\gamma: G_{\mathbb{Q}} \to \mathrm{GL}_2(R)$ of $\bar{\rho}$ such that for $\ell \neq p$ it is minimal in [D97]; if $k(\bar{\rho}) < p$, the restriction to $D_p$ comes from a Fontaine-Laffaille module; if $k(\bar{\rho}) = p+1$, restriction to $I_p$ is upper triangular with $\chi_p^{k-1}$ on the diagonal ($k = p+1$ crystalline, $k=2$ semistable).

nodes.name: Strictly compatible system
nodes.statement: A system of $\lambda$-adic representations of $\mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ such that, for every prime $q$, the Frobenius-semisimplification of the Weil-Deligne parameter at $q$ is isomorphic for all places $\lambda$ (including those with residue characteristic $q$); compatible drops the constraint at $\lambda$ over $q$.

nodes.name: Minimal strictly compatible system lifting $\bar{\rho}$
nodes.statement: A strictly compatible system $(\rho_\lambda)$ produced from a minimally ramified $\rho$ by Theorem \ref{minimal}, with prescribed good/semistable reduction outside $p$ matching the Artin conductor of $\bar{\rho}$.

nodes.name: Semistable representation $\bar{\rho}$
nodes.statement: $\bar{\rho}$ of Serre type is semistable if at primes outside $p$ ramification is unipotent and at $p$ the Serre weight $k(\bar{\rho}) \leq p+1$.

nodes.name: Existence of minimal $p$-adic lift (Theorem \ref{existminimallift})
nodes.statement: Let $p > 3$. Let $\bar{\rho}: G_{\mathbb{Q}} \to \mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{F})$ be odd absolutely irreducible with $2 \leq k(\bar{\rho}) \leq p+1$ and $k(\bar{\rho}) \neq p$. Then $\bar{\rho}$ has a lift $\rho$ minimally ramified at every $\ell$; if $k(\bar{\rho}) = p+1$ one may impose either crystalline type (weight $p+1$) or semistable type (weight 2).
conclusions: $\bar{\rho}$ admits a minimally ramified $p$-adic lift $\rho$
If $k(\bar{\rho}) = p+1$, both crystalline-type (weight $p+1$) and semistable-type (weight 2) minimal lifts exist

nodes.name: Universal deformation rings are finite flat complete intersections (Theorem \ref{completeinters})
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{existminimallift} with non-solvable image, $R_{\mathrm{univ}}$ (or both $R_{\mathrm{univ,crys}}$ and $R_{\mathrm{univ,ss}}$ when $k(\bar{\rho}) = p+1$) is a finite flat complete intersection $W$-algebra.
assumptions: Image of $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ under $\bar{\rho}$ is not solvable
conclusions: $R_{\mathrm{univ}}$ (or $R_{\mathrm{univ,crys}}, R_{\mathrm{univ,ss}}$ in weight $p+1$) is a finite flat complete intersection over $W$

nodes.name: Crystalline deformation ring is formally smooth (Proposition \ref{p+1})
nodes.statement: In the case $k(\bar{\rho}) = p+1$ (très ramifiée), the $W$-algebra $R_{p,\mathrm{crys}}$ is formally smooth of dimension 1.
conclusions: $R_{p,\mathrm{crys}} \simeq W[[T]]$, formally smooth of relative dimension 1

nodes.name: Finiteness criterion via finite image (Lemma \ref{finite})
nodes.statement: Let $\kappa$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$ and $G$ a profinite group satisfying the $p$-finiteness condition. For an absolutely irreducible $\eta: G \to \GL_N(\kappa)$ with universal deformation $\eta_{\mathcal{F}}: G \to \GL_N(R_{\mathcal{F}})$ in a deformation subcategory, $R_{\mathcal{F}}$ is finite iff $\eta_{\mathcal{F}}(G)$ is finite.
conclusions: $R_{\mathcal{F}}$ is finite if and only if $\eta_{\mathcal{F}}(G)$ is finite

nodes.name: Potential automorphy via Taylor (Proposition \ref{taylor})
nodes.statement: There exists a totally real field $F$ of even degree, unramified at $p$ (split at $p$ when $\bar{\rho}|_{D_p}$ is irreducible), with $\bar{\rho}|_{G_F}$ absolutely irreducible non-dihedral, unramified outside primes above $p$, and arising from a cuspidal automorphic form $\pi$ for $B_F$ of weight $k(\bar{\rho})$ and ordinary at primes above $p$ when $\bar{\rho}$ is ordinary; in weight $p+1$ also a Steinberg form $\pi'$ of weight 2.
conclusions: Existence of totally real $F$ of even degree with the listed properties (i)-(iii)
$\bar{\rho}|_{G_F}$ comes from a cuspidal automorphic form on $B_F$
Weight $p+1$ case: also a Steinberg form $\pi'$ of parallel weight 2

nodes.name: Potential irreducibility (Lemma \ref{potirr})
nodes.statement: Let $p > 2$ and $\eta: \mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q}) \to \mathrm{GL}_2(\bar{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ odd with non-solvable image. For any totally real Galois extension $F'/\mathbb{Q}$ and quadratic extension $F''/F'$, $\eta(G_{F''})$ is non-solvable; in particular $\eta|_{G_{F'}}$ is non-dihedral.
conclusions: $\eta(G_{F''})$ is not solvable
$\eta|_{G_{F'}}$ is non-dihedral

nodes.name: Minimal compatible system lifting semistable $\bar{\rho}$ (Theorem \ref{minimal})
nodes.statement: Let $\bar{\rho}$ be semistable of Serre type. Then $\bar{\rho}$ has a minimally ramified lift $\rho$ that, in case (i) (level 1, crystalline), fits into a compatible system $(\rho_\lambda)$ with controlled Weil-Deligne ramification, and in case (ii) (otherwise) fits into a strictly compatible system arising from étale cohomology of a variety over $\mathbb{Q}$, and when $k(\bar{\rho}) \in \{2, p+1\}$ from the Tate module of an abelian variety $A/\mathbb{Q}$.
conclusions: Existence of minimally ramified lift $\rho$ (crystalline of weight $k(\bar{\rho})$, or in weight $p+1$ also semistable of weight 2)
Case (i): compatible system $(\rho_\lambda)$ over a number field $E$, crystalline outside characteristic 2
Case (ii): strictly compatible system from étale cohomology; for $k(\bar{\rho}) \in \{2, p+1\}$ comes from $\lambda$-adic Tate module of an abelian variety $A/\mathbb{Q}$

nodes.name: Low-level Serre conjecture cases (Theorem \ref{lowlevel})
nodes.statement: (i) No irreducible finite flat group scheme of $(p,p)$ type over $\mathbb{Z}$; equivalently, no irreducible odd 2-dim $\bar{\rho}$ unramified outside $p$ with $k(\bar{\rho})=2$. (ii) For $p > 3$, no semistable $\bar{\rho}$ with prime-to-$p$ Artin conductor in $\{2,3,5,7,13\}$ and $k(\bar{\rho}) = 2$. (iii) For $p \in \{5,7,13\}$ no Serre type $\bar{\rho}$ unramified outside $p$ with $k(\bar{\rho}) = p+1$.
conclusions: (i) No irreducible $(p,p)$-type finite flat group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}$
(ii) No semistable $\bar{\rho}$ with conductor $\in \{2,3,5,7,13\}$ and weight 2
(iii) No Serre type $\bar{\rho}$ unramified outside $p \in \{5,7,13\}$ with $k=p+1$

nodes.name: Classification of $(p,p)$-type finite flat group schemes over $\mathbb{Z}$ (Corollary \ref{groupschemes})
nodes.statement: If $p$ is odd, the only $(p,p)$-type finite flat group schemes over $\mathbb{Z}$ are $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z} \oplus \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z} \oplus \mu_p$, or $\mu_p \oplus \mu_p$.
conclusions: Only $(p,p)$-type group schemes over $\mathbb{Z}$: $(\mathbb{Z}/p)^2$, $\mathbb{Z}/p \oplus \mu_p$, $\mu_p^2$

nodes.name: No level-1 Serre type in low weights (Theorem \ref{lowweight})
nodes.statement: There is no Serre type $\bar{\rho}$ of level 1 with $2 \leq k(\bar{\rho}) \leq 8$, or $k(\bar{\rho}) = 14$.
conclusions: No such $\bar{\rho}$ exists

nodes.name: Inexistence for small primes (Corollary \ref{small})
nodes.statement: For $p \in \{2,3,5,7\}$ there are no irreducible odd 2-dimensional mod $p$ representations of $\mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ unramified outside $p$.
conclusions: No irreducible odd 2-dim mod $p$ Galois representation unramified outside $p$

nodes.name: No irreducible crystalline $p$-adic representations in low weights (Theorem \ref{lowweight1})
nodes.statement: For odd $p$, there is no 2-dim odd irreducible $p$-adic representation of $\mathrm{Gal}$ unramified outside $p$ and crystalline of Hodge-Tate weights $(0,w)$ for $w \in \{1,3,5,7,13\}$ and $p \geq w$. Same for irreducible strictly compatible systems with good reduction everywhere.
assumptions: $w$ an odd number in $\{1,3,5,7,13\}$ with $p \geq w$
conclusions: No such 2-dim odd irreducible $p$-adic representation
No such irreducible strictly compatible system with good reduction everywhere

nodes.name: Weight-12 level-1 representations come from Ramanujan $\Delta$ (Theorem \ref{weight12})
nodes.statement: Let $\bar{\rho}$ be a Serre type, level 1 representation with Serre weight 12. Then $\bar{\rho}$ arises from the Ramanujan $\Delta$ function.
conclusions: $\bar{\rho}$ arises from the Ramanujan $\Delta$ function (mod $p$)

nodes.name: Crystalline weight-11 representations come from $\Delta$
nodes.statement: Any 2-dim irreducible $p$-adic representation $\rho$ unramified outside $p$ and crystalline of Hodge-Tate weights $(0,11)$ with $p \geq 11$ arises from the Ramanujan $\Delta$ function. Same for irreducible strictly compatible systems with good reduction everywhere of Hodge-Tate weights $(0,11)$.
assumptions: $\rho$ irreducible 2-dim $p$-adic, unramified outside $p$, crystalline of Hodge-Tate weights $(0,11)$
conclusions: $\rho$ arises from the Ramanujan $\Delta$ function

nodes.name: Classification of level-1 Serre type for $p = 11, 13$ and beyond (Corollary \ref{ugly})
nodes.statement: For $p = 11, 13$ the only level-1 Serre type $\bar{\rho}$ are twists of weight 12 (arising from $\Delta$) and weight-10 ones with non-semisimple local representation at $p$. For $p > 13$, certain enumerated Serre weights (e.g. $p-1, p-3, p-5, p-7, p-13$ in the locally split reducible case) admit no Serre type representations.
conclusions: Enumerated list of which Serre weights admit/do not admit such $\bar{\rho}$ at $p = 11, 13$ and beyond

nodes.name: Reduction of level-1 Serre conjecture to modularity lifting (Theorem \ref{bertrand})
nodes.statement: For every odd $p$, assume the modularity-lifting hypothesis for level-1 crystalline lifts of weight between 2 and $2p$ of either modular irreducible or reducible $\bar{\rho}$. Then Serre's conjecture in level 1 is true.
assumptions: Conditional: for every odd prime $p$, all crystalline lifts of weight $\in [2, 2p]$ of level-1 modular-or-reducible $\bar{\rho}$ are modular
conclusions: Serre's conjecture for all level-1 representations holds

nodes.name: Killing ramification: reduction of squarefree-conductor case to level 1 (Theorem \ref{levelone})
nodes.statement: For every odd $p$, assume modularity lifting for semistable lifts (outside $p$) of weight between 2 and $p+1$ at $p$ of squarefree-conductor modular-or-reducible $\bar{\rho}'$. Then Serre's conjecture for level 1 implies Serre's conjecture for all $\bar{\rho}$ ($p > 3$) with odd squarefree conductor prime to 3, determinant ramified only at $p$, and Serre weight either $p+1$ or at most 1 more than the least prime ramified in $\bar{\rho}$.
assumptions: Modularity lifting hypothesis for semistable lifts (squarefree conductor) of Serre weight in $[2, p+1]$
conclusions: Serre's conjecture holds for $\bar{\rho}$ (with $p > 3$) of odd squarefree prime-to-3 conductor, determinant ramified only at $p$, and the weight constraint

nodes.name: Serre's modularity conjecture
nodes.statement: Conjecture (Serre): every odd irreducible 2-dim mod $p$ representation $\bar{\rho}: \mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q}) \to GL_2(\mathbb{F})$ arises from a newform of optimal level and weight $(N(\bar{\rho}), k(\bar{\rho}))$ predicted by Serre's recipe.

nodes.name: Modularity lifting hypothesis (level-1 form)
nodes.statement: Prove that for every odd prime $p$, every continuous lift $\rho: \mathrm{Gal} \to \mathrm{GL}_2(\mathcal{O})$ of a level-1 modular-or-reducible $\bar{\rho}$, unramified outside $p$ and crystalline of weight $\in [2, 2p]$, is modular.

nodes.name: Modularity lifting hypothesis (squarefree-conductor form)
nodes.statement: Prove that for every odd $p$, every continuous lift $\rho'$ of a modular-or-reducible squarefree-conductor $\bar{\rho}'$ that is semistable outside $p$ and has Serre weight $\in [2, p+1]$ at $p$ is modular.

nodes.name: Böckle's complete intersection criterion
nodes.statement: If for each $\ell$ the local deformation rings $R_\ell$ are flat complete intersections of relative dimension $\dim_\kappa H^0(D_\ell, \mathrm{ad}^0 \bar{\rho}) + \epsilon_\ell$ ($\epsilon_p = 1$, else $0$), then $R_{\mathrm{univ}}$ has a CNL presentation $W[[X_1,\dots,X_r]]/(f_1,\dots,f_s)$ with $r \geq s$.

nodes.name: Taylor's potential automorphy theorem
nodes.statement: Theorem 5.7 of [T03] (supersingular case) and arguments of [T02] (ordinary case): for non-solvable $\bar{\rho}$, there exists a totally real $F$ over which $\bar{\rho}|_{G_F}$ becomes modular by an automorphic form on a totally definite quaternion algebra.

nodes.name: Skinner-Wiles modularity lifting (residually reducible / nearly ordinary)
nodes.statement: Modularity lifting for residually reducible representations and for nearly ordinary deformations of irreducible residual representations.

nodes.name: Wiles, Taylor-Wiles modularity lifting
nodes.statement: $R = T$ theorem: under suitable hypotheses, the universal deformation ring $R$ of a modular residual representation equals the corresponding Hecke algebra $T$, hence lifts are modular.

nodes.name: Schoof's classification of semistable abelian varieties
nodes.statement: There are no semistable abelian varieties over $\mathbb{Q}$ with good reduction outside one of $\{2,3,5,7,13\}$ (apart from those isogenous to powers of $J_0(N)$ for the relevant $N$).

nodes.name: Berger-Li-Zhu reductions of crystalline representations
nodes.statement: Reduction of irreducible crystalline 2-dim representations of $D_p$ of Hodge-Tate weights $(0,p)$ is an unramified twist of $\mathrm{ind}_{\mathbb{Q}_{p^2}}^{\mathbb{Q}_p}(\omega_2^p)$.

nodes.name: Bertrand's postulate
nodes.statement: For every $n \geq 1$ there is a prime $q$ with $n < q < 2n$. Equivalently, $p_{n+1} \leq 2p_n - 1$ for consecutive primes.

nodes.name: Fujiwara's $R = T$ for totally real fields
nodes.statement: Generalisation of Wiles' $R = T$ theorem to Hilbert modular forms over totally real fields in the ordinary case.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{existminimallift}
nodes.statement: Solvable image: handled by Langlands-Tunnell + Ribet's level/weight optimisation. Non-solvable: reduces to Theorem \ref{completeinters}, which gives the universal minimally ramified deformation ring is finite flat complete intersection, hence a $W$-point exists.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{completeinters}
nodes.statement: Apply Böckle's local-to-global complete intersection criterion combined with smoothness of local deformation rings (Ramakrishna, Taylor; Proposition \ref{p+1} for the crystalline-type ring at $p$ in weight $p+1$). Then prove $R_{\mathrm{univ}}/p$ is finite by reducing via Lemma \ref{finite} to finiteness of the image of $\bar{\rho}_{\mathrm{univ}}$ — which follows after base change to a totally real $F$ via Proposition \ref{taylor} from $R = T$ theorems.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition \ref{p+1}
nodes.statement: Use Lemma 29 of [DDT] to compute the relative cotangent space $\mathcal{M}/(p, \mathcal{M}^2)$ as a kernel of dimension 1 in Galois cohomology, so $R_{p,\mathrm{crys}}$ is a quotient of $W[[T]]$. Then exhibit infinitely many inequivalent crystalline-type liftings $D_p \to \GL_2(W)$ via inductive lifting modulo $p^{n+1}$ using Tate local duality and the très ramifiée hypothesis.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma \ref{finite}
nodes.statement: If $R_{\mathcal{F}}$ is finite, image is finite trivially. Conversely, by Carayol's theorem $R_{\mathcal{F}}$ is generated by traces of $\eta_{\mathcal{F}}(g)$. If image is finite, traces are sums of roots of unity, so each $R_{\mathcal{F}}/\wp$ is a finite extension of $\kappa$; hence $R_{\mathcal{F}}$ is dimension-0 noetherian, thus finite.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition \ref{taylor}
nodes.statement: Supersingular case is Theorem 5.7 of [T03]. Ordinary case: apply Moret-Bailly to construct an HBAV $A/E$ realising $\bar{\rho}$, use Lemma 1.5 of [T02] to verify ordinarity at primes above $p$, then use Conrad-Diamond-Taylor appendix B for the Weil-Deligne picture, Skinner-Wiles base change to clear away ramification, and Hida's weight-shifting (Section 8 of [Hida1]) to pass to weight $k(\bar{\rho})$. For weight 2, Mazur's principle (Jarvis Theorem 6.2) ensures the form can be chosen unramified everywhere.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma \ref{potirr}
nodes.statement: By Dickson's classification (Theorem 2.47 of [DDT]), the projective image $H \subset \mathrm{PGL}_2(\bar{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ is conjugate to $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_{p^r})$, $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_{p^r})$ ($p^r \neq 2,3$), or $A_5$. Restricting to $G_{F'}$ gives a non-trivial normal subgroup containing $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_{p^r})$ or $A_5$; since neither has a subgroup of index 2, restriction to $G_{F''}$ still contains it.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{minimal}
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem \ref{existminimallift} to obtain $\rho$. Use Theorem 6.6 of [T03] (Brauer's theorem) plus Arthur-Clozel base change to assemble $\rho$ into a weakly compatible system over a number field $E$. Promote to strict compatibility via Carayol-Taylor (places not above $q$), Breuil-Berger (case (i), crystallinity), and Saito (case (ii), Steinberg). Last statement of (ii) follows from Blasius-Rogawski + Galois descent + Faltings.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{lowlevel}
nodes.statement: Part (i): $p = 3$ by Serre [Serre2]; $p > 3$ by Theorem \ref{minimal} + Fontaine [Fontaine] (via [D], [Wint]). Part (ii): use Theorem \ref{minimal} for weight-2 minimal compatible lifts and Brumer-Kramer + Schoof to exclude semistable abelian varieties with the listed bad reduction. Part (iii): same after passing to weight-2 semistable lifting in the $k = p+1$ case.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary \ref{groupschemes}
nodes.statement: After Theorem \ref{lowlevel}(i) excludes irreducible $(p,p)$-type schemes, Serre's argument in Section 4.5 of [Serre3] gives the classification.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{lowweight}
nodes.statement: Even-weight observation; case-by-case for $k = 4, 6, 8, 14$, each handled by combining Theorem \ref{minimal} with [BLZ] (locally reducible at the auxiliary prime $\Rightarrow$ ordinary), Skinner-Wiles modularity lifting [SW2], and the inexistence of cusp forms of level 1 and the relevant weight ($\leq 8$ or $14$). Weight 6, 8: also use Schoof to rule out the $p = 5, 7$ cases.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{lowweight1}
nodes.statement: Set $k = w + 1$. If residually reducible, [BLZ] + [SW2] yields a level-1 form of weight $\leq 10$ or $14$ — none exist. If residually irreducible, build a compatible system via Theorem \ref{minimal} and look at the residue at the prime $w$: by [BLZ] the Serre weight there is $2$ or $w+1$, both ruled out by Theorem \ref{lowweight}. Done.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{weight12}
nodes.statement: By Corollary \ref{small} take $p \geq 11$. Apply Theorem \ref{minimal} to get a strictly compatible system of weight 12 with residual rep at $p$ being $\bar{\rho}$. Reduce mod 11: if reducible, [BLZ] + [SW2] finishes. Otherwise the 11-adic residual rep is très ramifiée (weight 12); apply Theorem \ref{existminimallift} for a weight-2 semistable lift, then Theorem \ref{minimal} produces an abelian variety $A$ semistable, good outside 11. Schoof says $A$ is isogenous to a power of $J_0(11)$, whose mod-11 representation matches $\Delta$ (Serre), so $\bar{\rho}_{11}$ comes from $\Delta$. Wiles modularity lifting then propagates this to the original compatible system.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{bertrand}
nodes.statement: Induction on the prime $p$. Base case $p = 7$: Corollary \ref{small}. Inductive step: given $\bar{\rho}$ mod $p_{n+1}$, build a compatible system via Theorem \ref{minimal} crystalline of weight $k(\bar{\rho}) \leq p_{n+1} + 1$. By Bertrand's postulate $p_{n+1} \leq 2 p_n - 1$, so the $p_n$-adic member of the compatible system has weight $\leq 2 p_n$ and is residually modular by induction hypothesis; the modularity-lifting assumption yields modularity, hence $\bar{\rho}$ is modular.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{levelone}
nodes.statement: Reduce $k = p+1$ to other allowed cases via Theorem \ref{minimal} and pass to a large auxiliary prime $q$. Then induct on $|S|$ where $S$ is the set of prime-to-$p$ ramification primes of $\bar{\rho}$. At each step apply Theorem \ref{minimal} to obtain a minimal strictly compatible system, look at its residue at the smallest ramification prime $q_1$; the new representation has strictly fewer prime-to-its-own-residue ramification primes and weight $\leq q_1 + 1$, so the inductive hypothesis applies. Use the modularity-lifting hypothesis to propagate modularity back.

nodes.name: Comparison with Ramakrishna's lifts
nodes.statement: Ramakrishna [R02] produced Witt-vector liftings (odd and even cases) by Galois cohomology, but they are rarely minimally ramified; the present approach via deformation rings + Taylor's potential automorphy gives minimal lifts but only in the odd case and without rationality control.

nodes.name: Simpler proof of Fermat's Last Theorem
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{lowlevel} yields a slightly simpler proof of Fermat's Last Theorem (avoiding the hardest of Ribet's level-lowering results, at least for $p > 49$, and avoiding the modularity of the putative weight-2, level-2 representation from a Fermat solution).

nodes.name: Conditional GRH refinement on conductor 6
nodes.statement: Assuming GRH and $p > 3$, Calegari [Calegari] yields no irreducible $\bar{\rho}$ with conductor 6 and Serre weight 2.

nodes.name: Why moderate-weight reduction matters
nodes.statement: The reduction to weights $\in [2, 2p]$ in Theorem \ref{bertrand} is technically critical because Breuil's conjectures on reductions of crystalline representations of weight at most $2p$ have a simple form and may be close to being proven.

nodes.name: Standing hypothesis on Serre weight range
nodes.statement: Throughout Section 2, $\bar{\rho}$ is assumed odd irreducible with Serre weight $2 \leq k(\bar{\rho}) \leq p + 1$ (always achievable by twisting by a power of $\bar{\chi}_p$).

nodes.name: Apply Böckle's local-to-global criterion
nodes.statement: Define for each prime $\ell$ the local versal deformation ring $R_\ell$ of $\bar{\rho}|_{D_\ell}$ with the prescribed minimal conditions. By Böckle's Proposition (appendix to [K03]), if each $R_\ell$ is a flat complete intersection of the prescribed relative dimension, then $R_{\mathrm{univ}}$ has a CNL presentation $W[[X_1,\dots,X_r]]/(f_1,\dots,f_s)$ with $r \geq s$.

nodes.name: Verify smoothness/CI for each local ring
nodes.statement: By Ramakrishna [R02] and Taylor [T03ico], $R_\ell$ is smooth over $W$ of the prescribed dimension except for $R_{p,\mathrm{crys}}$ in the $k = p+1$ case, which is a relative complete intersection of dimension 1 by Böckle (Proposition \ref{p+1}).

nodes.name: Reduce finiteness of $R_{\mathrm{univ}}$ to finite image
nodes.statement: By a standard regular-sequence argument it suffices to show $R_{\mathrm{univ}}/p R_{\mathrm{univ}}$ has finite cardinality. By Lemma \ref{finite} this reduces to showing $\bar{\rho}_{\mathrm{univ}}$ has finite image.

nodes.name: Local finite-ramification claim
nodes.statement: Claim: $\bar{\rho}_{\mathrm{univ}}$ is finitely ramified at every $\ell \neq p$, with $|\bar{\rho}_{\mathrm{univ}}(I_\ell)| = |\bar{\rho}(I_\ell)|$. Proof: when $\bar{\rho}|_{I_\ell}$ has unipotent part with character $\phi$, the universal lift's $\tilde{\phi}$ is tamely ramified (so cyclic) and killed by $p$ since $R_{\mathrm{univ}}/p$ is an $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra.

nodes.name: Base change to totally real $F$ via Proposition \ref{taylor}
nodes.statement: Choose $F$ as in Proposition \ref{taylor}. Let $\rho_{\mathrm{univ},F}$ be the corresponding universal minimal deformation of $\bar{\rho}|_{G_F}$. By the previous claim, $\bar{\rho}_{\mathrm{univ}}|_{G_F}$ is a specialisation of $\bar{\rho}_{\mathrm{univ},F}$, so it suffices to prove $\bar{\rho}_{\mathrm{univ},F}$ has finite image.

nodes.name: Apply Fujiwara/Taylor $R = T$ over $F$
nodes.statement: By Fujiwara's [Fujiwara] generalisation of $R = T$ to totally real fields (ordinary case) and Theorem 3.3 of [T03] (supersingular case), $R_{\mathrm{univ},F}$ is a finite $W$-module — it is identified with the completion of an ordinary Hida Hecke algebra. Hence $\bar{\rho}_{\mathrm{univ},F}$ has finite image, completing the proof.

nodes.name: Cotangent space is one-dimensional
nodes.statement: Identify the relative cotangent space $\mathcal{M}/(p, \mathcal{M}^2)$ with the kernel of $H^1(D_p, F^0) \to H^1(I_p, F^0/F^1)^{D_p/I_p}$, which has dimension 1 by Lemma 29 of [DDT] (using that $\bar{\rho}$ is très ramifiée). Hence $R_{p,\mathrm{crys}}$ is a quotient of $W[[T]]$.

nodes.name: Inductively construct lifts modulo $p^{n+1}$
nodes.statement: Given a crystalline-type lift $\rho_n: D_p \to \GL_2(W/p^n)$ in upper-triangular form with diagonal $(\delta, 1)$, construct lifts mod $p^{n+1}$ by perturbing $\delta$ by a character $\delta_\gamma$ with $\delta_\gamma(\sigma) = 1 + p^n \gamma(\sigma)$ for unramified $\gamma: D_p \to \mathbb{F}$.

nodes.name: Cup-product computation via Tate duality
nodes.statement: The connecting map $f_\gamma: H^1(W/p^n W(\delta)) \to H^2(\mathbb{F}(\bar{\chi}_p))$ is surjective by Tate local duality. The difference $f_\gamma(\eta) - f_0(\eta)$ is the cup product of $\gamma$ with $\bar{\eta}$; class field theory + très ramifiée property show this is non-zero for non-zero $\gamma$, so a unique $\gamma_1$ kills $f_{\gamma_1}(\eta)$.

nodes.name: Count inequivalent liftings, conclude isomorphism
nodes.statement: $|H^1(\mathbb{F}(\bar{\chi}_p))| = |\mathbb{F}|^2$ gives $|\mathbb{F}|$ inequivalent crystalline-type lifts modulo $p^{n+1}$, so $\bar{\rho}$ has infinitely many inequivalent $W$-lifts. A non-zero $f \in W[[T]]$ admits only finitely many maps $W[[T]]/(f) \to W$, so $R_{p,\mathrm{crys}} \simeq W[[T]]$.

nodes.name: Construct HBAV via Moret-Bailly
nodes.statement: Apply Moret-Bailly's theorem (as in [T02], p.137, ordinary case) to obtain an abelian variety $A$ over a totally real field $E$ of Hilbert-Blumenthal type with multiplication by a real field $M$, such that $\bar{\rho}|_{G_E}$ is realised on $A[\lambda]$ for some prime $\lambda$ of $M$ above $p$.

nodes.name: Verify ordinarity of $\pi_A$ at primes above $p$
nodes.statement: Use Lemma 1.5 of [T02] applied to $A$: since $k(\bar{\rho}) \neq p$, the parameter $n = p - k(\bar{\rho}) + 1$ (or 0 if $k = 2$) satisfies $0 \leq n < p - 1$ and $n \neq 1$. Conclude that $A$ has multiplicative or good reduction at primes above $p$ and $(\pi_A)_x$ is ordinary.

nodes.name: Weil-Deligne form via Conrad-Diamond-Taylor
nodes.statement: By appendix B of [CDT], the Weil-Deligne action $WD_x$ on the compatible system attached to $A$ factors through the Weil group as $\eta_1 \oplus \eta_2$ with $\eta_2$ unramified and $\eta_2(\mathrm{Frob}_x)$ a $\lambda$-adic unit, $\eta_1|_{I_x} = \omega^{-n}$. Thus $\pi_A$ is ordinary at $x$ with nebentypus $\Psi$ such that $\Psi \omega^{-n}$ is unramified.

nodes.name: Skinner-Wiles base change to clear ramification
nodes.statement: Use Skinner-Wiles base change [SW1] to a totally real solvable extension of $E$ unramified at primes above $p$, ensuring $\pi_A$ is unramified outside $p$ while remaining ordinary at primes above $p$.

nodes.name: Hida weight shifting to weight $k(\bar{\rho})$
nodes.statement: Apply Hida's weight shifting (Section 8 of [Hida1]; valid since $p > 3$ and $p$ is unramified in $F$): from the existence of ordinary $\pi_A$ of parallel weight 2, deduce that $\bar{\rho}$ arises from a cuspidal automorphic representation $\pi$ of $B_F(\mathbb{A}_F)$ of weight $(k(\bar{\rho}), \dots, k(\bar{\rho}))$, unramified at finite primes prime to $p$, ordinary at primes above $p$.

nodes.name: Mazur's principle for weight 2
nodes.statement: When $k(\bar{\rho}) = 2$, ensure $\pi$ has parallel weight 2 unramified at all finite places via Mazur's principle (Theorem 6.2 of [Jarvis]). Weight $p+1$ case: also exhibit a Steinberg form $\pi'$ of parallel weight 2.

nodes.name: Reduce to $p \geq 11$ via Corollary \ref{small}
nodes.statement: By Corollary \ref{small} no irreducible level-1 Serre type representations exist for $p \in \{2,3,5,7\}$, so we may assume $p \geq 11$.

nodes.name: Build weight-12 compatible system and reduce mod 11
nodes.statement: By Theorem \ref{minimal} obtain a strictly compatible system $(\rho_\lambda)$ with good reduction everywhere, crystalline of Hodge-Tate weights $(0,11)$, with residual representation at $p$ being $\bar{\rho}$. Reduce the 11-adic member modulo 11 to get $\bar{\rho}_{11}$.

nodes.name: Case split on reducibility of $\bar{\rho}_{11}$
nodes.statement: If $\bar{\rho}_{11}$ is reducible: apply Remark 4.1.2 of [BLZ] + Skinner-Wiles [SW2] to conclude modularity directly. Otherwise: $\bar{\rho}_{11}$ is irreducible and (by [BLZ]) très ramifiée of Serre weight 12.

nodes.name: Produce semistable weight-2 lift and abelian variety
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem \ref{existminimallift} to obtain another lift $\rho'_{11}$ of $\bar{\rho}_{11}$ that is unramified outside 11 and semistable at 11. By Theorem \ref{minimal}, $\rho'_{11}$ arises from an abelian variety $A/\mathbb{Q}$, semistable, with good reduction outside 11.

nodes.name: Identify $A$ with $J_0(11)$ via Schoof
nodes.statement: By Schoof [Schoof1] such an $A$ is isogenous to a power of $J_0(11)$. The mod-11 Galois representation of $J_0(11)$ is absolutely irreducible, ordinary at 11, and isomorphic (Théorème 11 of [Serre2]) to the mod-11 representation of $\Delta$, so $\bar{\rho}_{11}$ comes from $\Delta$.

nodes.name: Lift to compatible system via Wiles modularity
nodes.statement: The image of mod-11 $\Delta$ is all of $\GL_2(\mathbb{F}_{11})$ ([Serre4]), so Wiles modularity lifting [Wiles] (with [BLZ] giving ordinarity at 11) propagates modularity from $\bar{\rho}_{11}$ to the entire compatible system $(\rho_\lambda)$, hence to $\bar{\rho}$, which thus arises from $\Delta$.

nodes.name: Base case $p_0 = 7$
nodes.statement: By Corollary \ref{small} the level-1 Serre conjecture holds for $p \in \{2,3,5,7\}$, providing the induction base.

nodes.name: Inductive step: lift $\bar{\rho}$ at $p_{n+1}$ to compatible system
nodes.statement: Given $\bar{\rho}$ mod $p_{n+1}$, twist so $k(\bar{\rho}) \leq p_{n+1} + 1$. Apply Theorem \ref{minimal} to get a strictly compatible system $(\rho_\lambda)$ unramified everywhere, crystalline of weight $k(\bar{\rho})$, lifting $\bar{\rho}$ at a prime above $p_{n+1}$.

nodes.name: Bertrand's postulate + modularity lifting hypothesis
nodes.statement: Use Bertrand's postulate $p_{n+1} \leq 2 p_n - 1$ to bound the weight at the $p_n$-adic member of the compatible system by $2 p_n$. By the inductive hypothesis (Serre at $p_n$) the residual representation at $p_n$ is modular; the modularity-lifting assumption gives modularity of the $p_n$-adic lift, hence of the whole system, hence of $\bar{\rho}$.

nodes.name: Reduce $k = p+1$ case to other weights
nodes.statement: Use Theorem \ref{minimal} to lift $\bar{\rho}$ to a strictly compatible weight-2 semistable system. Pass to a large auxiliary prime $q$ where the $q$-adic member is crystalline of Hodge-Tate weights $(0,1)$ and residually irreducible; modularity of $\bar{\rho}_q$ implies modularity of the original via known modularity lifting.

nodes.name: Induct on the size of the ramification set $S$
nodes.statement: Order the prime-to-$p$ ramification primes as $S = \{q_1 < \cdots < q_n\}$. Base case: $S = \emptyset$ is the assumed level-1 Serre conjecture. Inductive step: apply Theorem \ref{minimal} to get a minimal compatible system at $\bar{\rho}$ of weight $k(\bar{\rho})$, look at its residue $\bar{\rho}_{Q_1}$ at a prime $Q_1$ over $q_1$.

nodes.name: Conclude via lifting hypothesis at each step
nodes.statement: $\bar{\rho}_{Q_1}$ has Serre weight $\leq q_1 + 1$ and (prime-to-$q_1$) Artin conductor strictly smaller than that of $\bar{\rho}$. By induction $\bar{\rho}_{Q_1}$ is modular, then by the modularity-lifting hypothesis $\rho_{Q_1}$ — and hence the whole compatible system — comes from a newform; this propagates back to $\bar{\rho}$.
